params.body:
Closes #1069

The support bell's Send button did nothing for French-speaking users. Its `onclick` passed the confirmation text to `custom.sendAnomaly('...')` inside single quotes; Blade escapes the apostrophe as `'`, the browser decodes it back before the handler runs, and the French "l'objet d'un suivi" ended the string. The handler was a syntax error, so no request went out. Dutch, English and German have no apostrophe there, which is why the bell kept working in Dutch accounts.

**What changes**
- `layouts/anomaly/index.blade.php`: the confirmation text goes to the script with `@js(trans(...))`, which quotes it for JavaScript (`'`).
- `settings/setting/_tabs/options.blade.php`: the reset-option-order button had the same fault in French (`l'affiche`, `l'ordre`); same fix.
- `TranslationsInClickHandlersTest`: renders the bell in nl, fr, en and de and checks the decoded handler is one JavaScript string; and a guard over every view that fails when a translation with a bare apostrophe sits inside a quoted inline handler. Without the fix both tests fail on exactly these two strings.
- Rule R P1-6.2 says the button works in every language and names the test.

Other handlers still quote `{{ trans(...) }}` by hand; none of their current translations has a bare apostrophe (`lblItemDupliceren` in French is pre-escaped as `l\'élément`), so they work, and the guard catches the next one. Dynamic values in those handlers (a vehicle name with an apostrophe) are not covered by the guard.

**Tests**: the new test, `RulesIdentityTest`, `CompiledViewsTest`, then the full suite: 3209 tests, OK. Pint passes on the new file.

Source: Portal mail:41.
params.title: The support bell sends in French: translations reach the script with @js
